passage: At the tuition verandah in Bhuj town, Rehana found a folded note tucked in her copy. It was from Zainab, in careful round letters: she liked Rehana as more than a friend. Rehana read it twice, her stomach knotting, and she thought about how easy it would be to smile, say nothing and enjoy being liked. But that wouldn't be fair. After class she asked Zainab to walk with her to the corner shop. "Thank you for telling me. It took courage," she said. "I care about you as my friend. But I don't feel the same way, and I don't want you hoping." Zainab swallowed and nodded. Rehana didn't tell anyone else, and the next day she sat beside her at tuition as usual.

qa.q: Where did Rehana find Zainab's note?
qa.a: She found it folded and tucked into her copy at the tuition verandah.

qa.q: What did Rehana think about before answering the note?
qa.a: She thought how easy it would be to smile, say nothing and enjoy being liked, but felt that wouldn't be fair to Zainab.

qa.q: What made Rehana's answer a kind and clear one?
qa.a: She thanked Zainab for her courage, said plainly she did not feel the same way, and kept it private, so there were no mixed signals and Zainab kept her dignity.

qa.q: How might Zainab have felt when she nodded?
qa.a: Hurt, since she swallowed before nodding, but also perhaps respected, because Rehana was honest and sat beside her the next day. 🤍

grounding: Rehana does not return a classmate's feelings and gives a kind, clear no, keeping her dignity and not leading her on.

After basketball practice, in the empty sports hall, Farah caught up with Jeevan. "Can I say something? I really like you. Like, like you."
Jeevan's stomach dropped. He liked Farah as a teammate, a good one. Nothing more.
Tushar had told him on Monday, "If she asks, just say maybe. Keep her around. It's nice being liked."
Jeevan took a breath. "Farah, thank you for telling me. That took guts. But I don't feel the same way. I'm sorry."
Farah's face fell. "Okay. That's clear."
"I still want to pass to you in the match on Friday," he said. "You're our best shooter."
She laughed shakily. "Obviously."
Later, when Tushar asked, Jeevan said only, "I told her no. Kindly. And that's all I'm saying." He didn't mention the details, and he never told anyone else.

qa.q: Where did Farah tell Jeevan she liked him?
qa.a: In the empty sports hall after basketball practice.

qa.q: How did Jeevan feel when Farah told him?
qa.a: His stomach dropped; he felt nervous and sorry, because he only saw her as a teammate.

qa.q: Why was Jeevan's reply better than Tushar's advice?
qa.a: A kind, clear no with no 'maybe' avoided mixed signals and leading Farah on, and keeping it private protected her dignity.

qa.q: How does Farah experience the rejection?
qa.a: She feels disappointed and a bit embarrassed, but the clear, kind answer lets her laugh and stay a teammate.

grounding: A teen liked by a teammate says a kind, clear no, protects her dignity and refuses to lead her on.

passage:
Dear Manjula,
I read your note three times. Thank you for trusting me with something so big. I know how brave that was.
I want to be honest, because you deserve that. I don't feel the same way about you. I care about you a lot as my friend, the one who shares her headphones on the bus and laughs at my terrible jokes. But it isn't more than that for me.
I'm not going to tell anyone about your note. Not a single person. It's yours.
I know things might feel strange for a while. If you want some space, I understand. If you still want to sit together on the bus, I'd really like that. I don't want to give you mixed signals, so I'm saying it clearly now instead of being vague.
You're a wonderful person. That hasn't changed.
Kashish

qa.q: What does Manjula share with Kashish on the bus?
How does Kashish seem to feel while writing the letter?
qa.a: Kashish feels caring but careful, and a little worried about hurting Manjula, which is why the letter is so gentle.

qa.q: What makes Kashish's letter a kind and clear no?
qa.a: It says plainly there are no romantic feelings, promises privacy, offers space or continued friendship, and avoids mixed signals.

qa.q: How might Manjula feel reading the letter?
qa.a: She may feel hurt and disappointed, but also respected, because Kashish kept her secret and treated her with dignity.

grounding: A teen who does not return a friend's feelings gives a kind, clear no, keeps her dignity and avoids mixed signals.
